entries.snippet: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

entries.snippet: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

entries.snippet: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

entries.snippet: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in President Donald Trump's White House.

entries.title: Work has stopped on system that was key to Trump effort to limit mail voting, USPS chief says
entries.snippet: The top official at the U.S. Postal Service said Thursday that the agency has stopped work on developing a controversial computer system that was central to President Donald Trump's effort to limit mail voting after the Supreme Court rejected his executive order this week.

entries.title: Man who sprayed Rep. Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months in prison
entries.snippet: The man who sprayed vinegar at Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar during a Minneapolis town hall was sentenced Thursday to 14 months in prison after reaching a deal with prosecutors.

entries.snippet: Using fossilized teeth, scientists have finally taken the T. rex's temperature — and it wasn't too different from our own.

entries.title: Trump's push to restrict mail ballots failed. Other efforts to reshape the midterms continue
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court this week closed the chapter on one of Trump's effort to dramatically overhaul of the nation's mail voting processes. But the case was just one example of the Republican president's numerous attempts to assert federal control over the upcoming midterms.

entries.title: Wheelchair tennis celebrates 50 years and a new wave of popularity

entries.title: Jon Ronson and Geoff Bennett discuss modern masculinity on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: Jon Ronson's new book, "The Castle," asks questions about what young men are being taught about what it means to be a man. Ronson joined Geoff Bennett on our PBS News podcast "Settle In" and discussed why certain visions of masculinity are proving so powerful right now.

entries.title: Tens of thousands flee as Iran-backed Houthis draw Yemen into wider war
entries.snippet: An estimated 125,000 people have fled as Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced down the Red Sea coast to a key maritime chokepoint.

entries.title: Jon Kyl, long-serving lawmaker from Arizona who shaped water policy, dies at 84
entries.snippet: Kyl spent almost three decades in Congress, serving in both chambers, and watched his party undergo a drastic transformation, with his career spanning Ronald Reagan's presidency to President Donald Trump's first term.

entries.title: Judge orders Kennedy Center to provide 30 days' notice before making any major physical changes
entries.snippet: The Kennedy Center's Trump-aligned board, chaired by the president, voted to close the center after U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper blocked the institution from returning President Donald Trump's name to the building.

entries.title: Climate change made deadly Nepal glacier and rock collapse more likely, analysis finds
entries.snippet: Human-caused global warming thinned glaciers and thawed mountain permafrost, likely helping to destabilize the Himalayan slope that collapsed last month and unleashed catastrophic flooding across Nepal, according to a report released Thursday.

entries.title: About 35 million people have been put into new House districts in the fight over congressional maps, report says
entries.snippet: The findings display the stark overhaul that partisan redistricting fights kicked off by President Donald Trump last year have caused for Americans across the country.

entries.title: A global AI safety strategy depends on U.S.-China cooperation. They each see the other as the problem

entries.title: Philippines: At least 3 students killed in school shooting
entries.snippet: Emergency services received reports of gunfire at the Banga National High School in southern Mindanao on Friday afternoon. At least three students were killed, including the suspected gunman.

entries.title: Germany news: Fuel costs dominate debate ahead of polls
entries.snippet: Germany's coalition government is grappling with record high fuel prices ahead of two state elections this weekend. Follow DW for more stories making headlines in Germany.

entries.title: India: Are food safety rules too much to swallow?
entries.snippet: Recent raids at India's luxury hotels and a wider crackdown on its food companies have renewed the debate about food safety standards and their enforcement in the country.

entries.title: India heads for driest monsoon in 17 years as El Nino curbs rainfall
entries.snippet: El Nino has put India on track for its driest monsoon since 2009. Meanwhile, the Election Commission has barred both Trinamool factions from using the party's name in by-elections. More with DW.

entries.title: Nigeria: Protests erupt over deaths of 37 miners in custody
entries.snippet: Dozens of suspects accused of illegal mining were found dead in custody in Nigeria's north-central Niger State. Officials blame disease, while reports cite overcrowding and poor ventilation.

entries.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
entries.snippet: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

entries.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
entries.snippet: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

entries.title: Bolivia: New cat species discovered by scientists
entries.snippet: Genetic data confirmed that the small feline, called "tilcayo" by locals, is a new species of cat. It's the first such discovery in more than 100 years.

entries.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
entries.snippet: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

entries.title: Australia: Man killed in shark attack near Perth
entries.snippet: A swimmer was mauled by a shark, with witnesses reporting a massive pool of blood in the water. There have been four confirmed fatal shark attacks in Australia this year.

entries.title: Venezuela unblocks some news websites censored for years
entries.snippet: Venezuela has restored access to 17 news sites that were blocked for years under Nicolas Maduro's administration. While activists welcomed the move, they noted that dozens more news portals, remain inaccessible.

entries.title: Malaysia: Jailed ex-leader Najib allowed house arrest
entries.snippet: Convicted in the 1MDB scandal for embezzling millions, former Prime Minister Najib Razak had repeatedly sought clemency. Malaysia's king has now granted him a "conditional pardon."

entries.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
entries.snippet: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

entries.title: Organized crime and drug-related deaths rise Germany
entries.snippet: Presenting its annual report for organized crime, the German police said that cocaine was a danger for the state and society, and that the cases of money laundering had increased.

entries.title: Russia votes for new parliament in controlled elections
entries.snippet: Russia is holding elections for the State Duma for the first time since Moscow sent troops into Ukraine in 2022. The party of President Vladimir Putin is expected to win the highly controlled affair.

entries.title: Aztec manuscript returns to Mexico after two centuries, on loan
entries.snippet: For years, Mexico has demanded the return of a treasured manuscript. Now the Aztec relic is back home from France — but on loan.

entries.title: UN mission notes possible US war crimes in Iran strikes
entries.snippet: A United Nations fact-finding mission said it found "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed war crimes in two airstrikes in Iran.

entries.title: Trump hails 'major progress' in setting up US base in Poland
entries.snippet: The location of the permanent US military base in Poland could be announced "very soon," Donald Trump has said. The US president also praised the leadership of his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki.

entries.title: US: Trump administration weakens Endangered Species Act
entries.snippet: In a recent memo, the US government would no longer consider the unintentional killing of protected wildlife as unlawful.
